svg.text: Shinegle low voltage: key, F-N-R, throttle, sensors, programmer
Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'sg'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: S01: KIT_KEY.out -> ESTOP.in - Without the e-stop, KIT_KEY goes straight to the lock relay or J1-1
S03: RELAYS2.NC2 -> SG1202.J1-1 - KSI through 10 A fuse (manual). NC contact so a dead control box never strands you
S04: KIT_KEY.out -> FNR.COM - Manual feeds the direction switch from the key
S11: SG1202.J1-25 -> MOTOR.SPD_12V - Speed sensor plugs J6/J7
S15: MOTOR.TEMP1 -> SG1202.J1-8 - Motor temp plugs J8/J9
S17: SG1202.J1-6 -> SPEEDO.SPD - Speed pulse. Could also feed the Pico if CAN isn't fitted
S18: SG1202.J3 -> PROG.PLUG - Setup only. J3 to J1-25/28/29/7 TBC
SG1202: Shinegle SG1202 controller - Full J1 pinout in config/shinegle-sg1202.yaml and docs/img/sg1202-wiring.svg
RELAYS2: 2-ch relay board - Relay 9 steering enable, relay 10 drive lock (uses the NC contact)
FNR: F-N-R switch - Physical switch straight to the controller. The reverse side is also tapped for the control box
PROG: SG1810 handheld programmer - Only plugged in for setup. Carries 12 V, never into USB
ESTOP: E-stop button - For RC mode. In series with KSI so it cuts drive with no software
KIT_KEY: Shinegle kit key switch - The kit comes with its own key switch. Is it the Teryx key, or a second one?
